newsitem.title: UK: Brazil stirs faintly in becalmed LDC debt market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stirs faintly in becalmed LDC debt market.

text.p: Only Brazilian debt showed any spark of life in a thin emerging debt market, with traders looking for prices to continue their upwards drift into the year end.
"Volumes are practically zero -- we've got the year-end in a couple of days and our dealers are saying don't rock the boat, just let the market go up," said one trader at a European firm in London.
Brazil was about the only Latin American credit to stir in the quiet inter-holiday period, its C bonds edging up 1/4 point to 74-1/2 from Friday's close.
But the trader said the move was sentiment-based and not inspired by any market-moving news.
Peruvian paper was flat and one trader said the pressure was starting to ease as the embassy hostage crisis moved into its 13th day. Peru Non-Citi debt was steady at 116-00.
Russian paper meanwhile drifted a touch higher in line with the market's generally firm tone. Dollar Vnesh loans touched 80-1/4 at 1230 GMT after closing at 79-3/4 on Friday.

Bulgarian IABs inched up 1/8 to 51-7/8, struggling to regain some of the ground it lost amid last week's political crisis surrounding the resignation of prime minister Zhan Videnov. A replacement has yet to be chosen.
Most traders are pinning their hopes on an influx of fresh cash in the new year, looking for a inflow of crossover money after a strong market performance in 1996.
The JP Morgan emerging bond index was up 14.71 percent over the year to date, and up 0.03 percent day-on-day at 124.55. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
